title: Clinical Masterclass: The Quiet Unilateral Proptosis
summary: Unilateral proptosis in a quiet, non-inflamed eye is a diagnostic challenge requiring a systematic anatomical approach to differentiate orbital space-occupying lesions. This guide prioritizes clinical vigilance and precision imaging to localize pathology from the cavernous sinus to the orbital apex.

sections.title: Red Flags: Urgent Investigations
content: Presence of optic nerve compressive signs (APD, dyschromatopsia)
History of systemic neoplasm (breast, lung, prostate, melanoma)

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup Sequence
content: Step 1: Complete slit-lamp and dilated fundoscopy.
Step 3: Forced Duction Testing to evaluate motility restriction.
Step 4: Imaging: MRI Orbit with/without fat suppression (Gold Standard).
Step 5: CT Orbits (Bone windows for remodeling).
Step 6: Systemic workup (Thyroid function tests, Ig-G4, biopsy).

content.explanation: V: Vascular (Hemangioma), I: Inflammatory (TED, IgG4), T: Traumatic, A: Autoimmune, M: Metabolic, I: Infectious/Iatrogenic, N: Neoplastic, S: Systemic

sections.title: Clinical Pearls for the Examination
content: Always auscultate the globe if the eye is quiet to rule out low-flow carotid-cavernous fistulas.
A 'quiet' eye with proptosis is a hallmark of low-grade, slow-growing tumors (e.g., cavernous hemangioma).
Fat suppression is mandatory on MRI to distinguish orbital fat from infiltrative masses.
Inferior displacement suggests a superior orbital mass (e.g., lacrimal gland tumor).
Always evaluate for eyelid retraction, which strongly points towards thyroid eye disease even in unilateral presentation.
